title: The Saviour Gently Calls
description: The Saviour Gently Calls in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 669 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Christ calling Children to Himself”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The Sa-viour gen-tly calls Our child-ren to his breast; He folds them in his gra-cious arms; Him-self de-clares them blest.

lines: He folds them in his gracious arms;
The heirs of heaven are such as these, —
For such as these I came."
Imploring, that, as we are thine,

licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
